title: Sympathetic and vagal in one plot: the cardiac autonomic indices (a newly-authored op), bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2

dataset.name: Fantasia Database
dataset.record: subject f1y01 (young), first 5-min RR window (391 intervals); aging comparison uses all 10 subjects
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271(4):R1078-R1084. Fantasia Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The Poincare plot's 4-SD bounding box (long axis L = 4*SD2, short axis T = 4*SD1) yields two clinically-used cardiac autonomic indices (Toichi 1997): the Cardiac Sympathetic Index (CSI = L/T) and the Cardiac Vagal Index (CVI = log10(L*T)). The ecosystem had the raw SD1/SD2 but not these indices; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, ecgHRVautonomic, that computes CSI/CVI/CSI_Modified. On a real 5-minute RR window it reproduces NeuroKit2's hrv_nonlinear indices BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0), and the finding: the Cardiac Vagal Index is higher in the young (4.90) than the old (4.55), robust across the cohort (5/5 young above the old mean) -- the parasympathetic decline of autonomic aging.

claims.statement: Cardiac Sympathetic Index (CSI = L/T = SD2/SD1) -- sympathetic predominance marker
Cardiac Vagal Index (CVI = log10(L*T)) -- parasympathetic (vagal) activity marker
Modified CSI (L^2/T) -- a more sensitive sympathetic marker (seizure detection)
mean Cardiac Vagal Index across the 5 young subjects
mean Cardiac Vagal Index across the 5 old subjects -- lower (vagal decline with age)
young subjects (of 5) with CVI above the old mean -- robustness of the vagal-decline finding

validation.reference: The newly-authored ecgHRVautonomic op is validated against NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear. NeuroKit2 re-computes the Toichi cardiac autonomic indices (CSI/CVI/CSI_Modified) from the same RR (peaks reconstructed from the integer-ms RR at 250 Hz so NeuroKit2 sees the identical series). The agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0) because the op uses SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) (universal) and SD2 = the geometric paired-projection (the Toichi/NeuroKit2 convention) and applies the identical L/T formulas. The finding: CVI (vagal index) is higher in the young (4.90) than the old (4.55), 5/5 young above the old mean.
validation.data: REAL -- Fantasia (PhysioNet), subject f1y01 5-min RR for the certified op; all 10 subjects for the aging comparison
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored ecgHRVautonomic reproduces NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear's CSI/CVI/CSI_Modified bit-for-bit (max |diff| 0); (2) CVI (vagal) is higher in young (4.90) than old (4.55), 5/5 young above the old mean. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a genuine gap -- the ecosystem had the raw SD1/SD2 (ecgHRVpoincare) but not the clinical Toichi CSI/CVI indices; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op uses the identical Toichi L/T formulas with SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) and SD2 = the geometric paired-projection (the convention in which CSI/CVI are defined, matching NeuroKit2), so the residual is 0; NOTE the geometric SD2 differs by a small O(1/n) amount from ecgHRVpoincare's analytical closed-form SD2 (the CSI/CVI convention is the geometric one); (3) the finding -- CVI declines with age -- is the expected parasympathetic decline of autonomic aging, complementing the DFA (alpha1 rises) and Poincare (SD1 falls) aging results on the SAME cohort; the CSI (sympatho-vagal ratio) is comparatively stable; descriptive on n=5+5, not a clinical claim; (4) a 5-min window of one subject for the certified op; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic closed form).

open_questions.q: CSI_Modified is the marker Jeppesen (2014) used for seizure detection from single-lead ECG; computing it in a sliding window over an ictal recording -- and pairing it with the DFA alpha1 and HRA on the same beats -- would test the multi-index autonomic signature of seizures. Documented, not escalated.
